title: Machine learning screening reveals ABBV-744 as a modulator of P2Y purinergic receptors
summary: Researchers used consensus machine-learning classifiers trained on known P2Y6 agonists to select compounds for pharmacological testing. The anticancer drug ABBV-744 showed non-surmountable inhibition of UDP-induced P2Y6 receptor activation and enhanced P2Y1 receptor activation in cellular assays, revealing previously unreported purinergic-receptor activity for this molecule.
ai_technology: Consensus of deep learning, AdaBoost, naive Bayes, k-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, random forest, SVM and XGBoost classifiers
organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases and Collaborations Pharmaceuticals

evidence.tested: Researchers used consensus machine-learning classifiers trained on known P2Y6 agonists to select compounds for pharmacological testing.
evidence.unknown: The paper found no novel P2Y6 agonists, which was the initial aim. ABBV-744 inhibited P2Y6 activation at relatively high micromolar concentration (reported IC50 about 75.7 µM); its precise inhibitory mechanism was not determined and requires further assays. P2Y1 enhancement and weak P2Y14 binding effects are assay-specific observations, not clinical pharmacology or therapeutic benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Models trained on curated P2Y6 agonist activity data prioritized molecules from compound libraries for experimental screening. Functional calcium-transient assays in receptor-expressing cells and fluorescent binding assays were used to test predictions; ABBV-744 was the principal confirmed hit with unanticipated activity across P2Y receptor subtypes.
